abstract: The last row of RAMA, the inverse of the floor-quotient matrix ARH, is the sequence of sums of the Möbius function over the blocks of integers d with the same quotient of n by d. Its sum is the Mertens function, and the sum of its absolute values is the quantity of the Croatian Conjecture: that it never exceeds Dirichlet's divisor sum taken at the number of floor quotients of n, and that the quotient of the two has a limit. The conjecture is stronger than what the Riemann Hypothesis is known to give, and we do not prove it. This paper collects what can be said about that row without any hypothesis. We recall the Euler product of the dilation matrices and its local equations, state the conjectures, and prove: the right half of the row consists of single values of the Möbius function, so that its part of the absolute sum is a count of squarefree integers; each entry has the parity of the number of squarefree integers in its block; the row at n and the row at n plus one differ by an explicit move of the values of the Möbius function at the divisors, found by nepo_mathematician; the rows of the partial Euler products obey an exact recursion in the number of primes, and no bound uniform in the vector can pass the order of n; the last row is the unique solution of a finite form of the approximation problem of Nyman and Beurling. The main result rests on a theorem of Tao: on the columns just below the square root of n, the mean square of the row equals the count of squarefree integers, in logarithmic mean. Nine rows are worked out in full at the end.
author: lasic_oblak
title: On the road to the Croatian Conjecture: a theorem of Terence Tao as a lighthouse for the last row of RAMA
